cells.tense: You are here now, and the thinking is moving well with you.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something small today without a plan for where it ends — a page, a call, a first move. Let starting be enough.
cells.core:
Right now this works. Something arrives half-formed — a problem without edges, an idea still wet — and by the time you've talked it through, it has a shape. Your mind moves fast and cuts what's cluttering the call. People bring you the tangle and leave with the clean line.

You shine because something in you finished growing, not because you're working at shine. What feeds it next is starting something a little too early. The next idea that hooks you — begin it before you know the destination. Follow the direction a while without needing to know how it ends. The fire has its own clock and it doesn't need a route yet.
cells.sheetLine: You cut to the clean line, and the room feels lighter.
cells.verb: cutting through fog with speed and precision
cells.place: the doorway where what's arriving first shows up

cells.tense: You will be braced for a future that cannot be written in ahead of time.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Stop circling the decision you've already weighed. Take the single step today that commits you to it, then leave it alone.
cells.core:
Something is being pushed ahead of its clock. An idea gets sped up before it has cooked, so thinking has to arrive already formed. You're watching for what's entering before you know its shape, and watching turns into steering.

The fix isn't more analysis. It's one decisive act made now that cuts the circling short — a call you've turned over long enough that making it is the only piece left. Not a direction for your life, a move for this. Afterward, let the quiet hold what you decided. You'll know you're back when the answer fits and whoever's in it tells you so.
cells.sheetLine: You finish the answer before the question has landed.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Show what you know by doing it beside someone — cook it together, walk it together, fix it together. Let them watch your hands.
cells.core:
When it's going well, this is a person who hears a muddle and names the part that matters, fast, and the muddle settles. You see the shape of a thing before anyone else in the conversation does, and you say it plain. That's the knack, and it's yours.

Lately it has gone quiet. What arrives gets left where it lands, and the shape goes unread. Forcing the thinking back won't work. You get it moving by doing something beside another person, hands on the work, feeling it while you go. Energy comes back through the doing, not the analyzing.
cells.sheetLine: You knew what you were looking at, and called it nothing.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where you are already writing.
cells.act: be present to their feeling without drowning in it
cells.ask: Stay with someone you love while they feel something hard, ten minutes, without fixing it. Notice what happens when you don't tidy it.
cells.core:
You are already doing it. Something arrives — a person's confusion, a group's stuckness — and it gets cleared fast, cleanly, wherever you are standing. If asked, you did nothing and it cleared itself. But it keeps happening near you.

The author has stepped out of the writing. That's the piece. Sit beside one person while they feel something hard, and just be there. Don't read it for them, don't organize it. Let the feeling run without you tidying it, and notice what shows up when you don't. Ten minutes of staying. No verdict needed, no clean line. Just presence beside them.
cells.sheetLine: You think it clears itself. It only does when you're near.
